topic: Clouds weigh hundreds of tonnes. Why don't they fall?
lesson: A cloud really is hundreds of tonnes and really is falling, but its droplets are so small that air resistance slows them to a crawl and rising warm air pushes them back up.

post.caption:
A cumulus cloud weighs around 500 tonnes, and it is falling right now. Its droplets are millionths of a metre across, so air resistance slows them to about a centimetre per second while warm air rises past them faster. Rain is what happens when droplets merge and finally win.
